claim_decisions.uncertainty: Modeled flood-loss shares relative to regional GDP, not observed regional loss counts or a complete marz ranking; asset values affect estimates.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2024-10 reports: Lori and Tavush hosted 7% of Nagorno-Karabakh refugees before the May 2024 floods; refugees and host households in Tashir and Alaverdi faced flood-related displacement and damage to homes, food supplies and essential services.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Historical PDNA context: the 7% refugee-hosting share concerns Lori and Tavush together before the May 2024 flood, not each locality or current populations; host and refugee flood impacts are not conflict attribution.

claim_decisions.uncertainty: Focus-group/field-discussion account of registration-related compensation barriers for women-headed households; missing disaggregated data preclude a measured prevalence.

gaps: Conflict-affected farmland rehabilitation and shared restoration/water management are stated response objectives, not demonstrated reduced competition or stronger cohesion.
Named refugee/host flood impacts and registration-related recovery barriers provide differentiated vulnerability evidence without implying that climate caused the displacement conflict.
No complete climate→violence or verified reverse operational insecurity pathway is assembled from these sources.

executive_assessment.text: Named marz crop/water risks and Lori–Tavush flood impacts distinguish exposure and vulnerability. PDNA evidence highlights displaced and host households and registration-related recovery barriers for women-headed households.

Older adaptation/crop-insurance plans and the 2026–2030 framework describe intended institutional and peace/resilience capacities; elapsed plan deadlines and future cohesion objectives are not verified results.
